# Working with an AI coding assistant as a daily engineering partner

> Plain-text knowledge base: a general method for one engineer and one AI assistant running a daily plan / execute / review loop on a real software project, with the rules, lessons and tips that came out of three months of it. Examples omit client and internal project identifiers; the public author's licence attribution is retained. Everything is written to be reused by any team.

## Core
- [WORKFLOW.md](WORKFLOW.md): the daily loop (plan, fresh executor sessions, end-of-day review), predicates, controls in order of trust, estimates measured
- [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md): working rules with reasons; read before acting in this style
- [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md): failure classes in what happened / cause / fix / prevention form
- [VERIFICATION.md](VERIFICATION.md): the false-green family — record the mechanism behind a pass, make success distinguishable from a not-yet-started world, prove a check can fail, measure the outcome and not the gate, let a missing thing stay a finding
- [TIPS.md](TIPS.md): general tips for working with an AI assistant, each with why and how

## Reuse
- [templates/lesson.md](templates/lesson.md): the lesson format
- [templates/review.schema.json](templates/review.schema.json): JSON schema of the end-of-day review, including estimate vs actual
- [templates/day-plan.schema.json](templates/day-plan.schema.json): JSON schema of the day plan, including the two estimates
- [tools/publish-check.sh](tools/publish-check.sh): the push-time gate that keeps project-specific terms out of this repository
